text:
Pittsburgh had a two-goal lead by 8:57 of the first period and spent the rest of the night watching it dissolve. Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust scored 29 seconds apart, and PIT led the first period in expected goals, 1.60 to 0.82. Then Artturi Lehkonen cut it to 2-1 at 11:01, and Colorado took over.

The second period decided it. COL out-chanced PIT 2.25 to 0.90 in expected goals, and Lehkonen tied the game 25 seconds in with a backhand off a 39 percent look. Gabriel Landeskog made it 3-2 at 4:24, and T.J. Hughes pushed it to 4-2 at 14:57. Mackenzie Blackwood had a quiet but effective night at the other end, stopping 30 of 32 shots and saving 1.34 goals more than the chances deserved. Arturs Silovs allowed five on 4.50 expected, a modest gap, which says most of this was Colorado creating better looks rather than Pittsburgh's goalie falling apart.

Nathan MacKinnon made it 5-2 on a third-period power play at 15:06, his only goal of a night in which he also had three assists and nine shots on goal. With him on the ice, COL held a 4.00 to 0.97 expected goals edge. Nazem Kadri had the best miss, a 50 percent chance that Silovs stopped. COL deserved to win 68 percent of the time, and it did so while PIT was held without a power-play goal on three chances.
